prize_parts.citation: For the theoretical prediction of flat bands at a magic twist angle in bilayer graphene and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene

statement.case_for: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene is a new quantum behaviour in a carbon-only material, tuned by a purely geometric parameter, the twist angle. The Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model gave a quantitative, falsifiable prediction of flat bands at a specific angle. The 2018 experiments by the Jarillo-Herrero group then found correlated insulators and superconductivity at that angle, in a system many theorists would not have expected to behave this way. This is the theory-meets-measurement structure I value, and it echoes the graphene lesson that experiment can overturn what we thought we knew. It also opened a whole field of moire materials that independent groups worldwide have entered, with tunable correlated phases in a single device. In my own field, continuum and first-principles band-structure calculations were quickly shown to be quantitatively relevant to the measured spectra.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation, pressed by several colleagues, is maturity. The pairing mechanism of the superconductivity is unsettled, twist-angle disorder and sample-to-sample variability complicate reproducibility, and the field is under a decade old. If the committee wants a stable interpretation of the full phenomenon, B007 (topological insulators) or B042 (optical lattice clocks) are better consolidated. There is also a real attribution problem: the experimental first authors (Cao, Fatemi) are not among the credited names, and earlier theory work (for example Lopes dos Santos, Peres and Castro Neto, and Santos and Peres) is not credited.

responses.point: Eva Lindroth ranks B054 last of her listed candidates because the origin of the superconductivity and correlated states is still debated, so the interpretation is not stable and recognition may be early.
responses.response: I take this seriously and it is my own main worry. I would separate two claims, though. The existence of the flat bands, the correlated insulating states and the superconducting domes has been reproduced by many independent groups and is stable. What is open is why the superconductivity occurs. Past prizes have recognised discoveries whose microscopic explanation was incomplete when they were awarded, and the citation can be limited to the prediction and the experimental discovery of the phases. I would ask the committee to verify that sample dependence does not undermine the claim that the phases are intrinsic.

responses.point: Goran Johansson places B042 first as a highly mature, widely reproduced piece of precision metrology, and puts B054 seventh on possible prematurity relative to longer-matured candidates.
responses.response: I agree that lattice clocks are very mature, and I am open to B042 as a strong fallback, so I have listed it as an alternative. My hesitation is that I rank it seventh because I cannot judge the AMO attribution well. I would still ask whether the discovery is a new state or behaviour of matter or mainly a measurement achievement, and how far it overlaps with the 2005 and 2012 prizes. I think B054 gives more new physics per unit time, but I do not think the clock case is weak, and I would not oppose it if the AMO members find the attribution clean.

responses.point: Bernhard Mehlig ranks B007 first and B054 third. He values the clean, analysable Bistritzer-MacDonald mechanism but notes the interpretation of the correlated phases is not stable and that the credited names do not cover all junior experimentalists.
responses.response: We agree that the continuum model is the kind of simple, quantitative insight that makes a prize defensible, and I am glad he separates the flat-band prediction from the full phenomenon. On B007 I agree on quality, since I ranked it third. My concern is that the 2016 prize on topological phases overlaps conceptually and that Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang and Fu fall outside the credited names, which leaves the allocation exposed. I would put B007 second and not first for that reason. I also keep the laureate set at two for B054, because Bistritzer was a postdoc and the experimental credit is better handled by crediting the group leader.

responses.point: Eva Olsson ranks B056 (aberration-corrected electron microscopy) first as a mature instrument that opened a door, and puts B054 third with the caveat that the experimental credit omits junior authors.
responses.response: I share her view that observation-enabling instruments matter, and as a theorist I use atomic-resolution TEM results as input to my own spectra. My difficulty with B056 is the physics-versus-instrumentation balance she herself flags: this prize is for physics, and the case should rest on a discovery about nature. On B054 I accept her point about junior experimentalists. The Nobel limit of three and the committee's practice of crediting the group leader make this unavoidable, but I would record it explicitly in the committee statement.

responses.point: Ulf Danielsson ranks B054 seventh, calling it natural as theory plus experiment but probably early given the unresolved mechanism and the short track record, and puts experimental Higgs, black-hole imaging and neutrinos higher.
responses.response: I defer to him and Mark Pearce on particle and astro matters, which are far from my area. I still think the argument that the field is under ten years old needs weighing against the speed and breadth of independent confirmation. I would ask whether the collaboration-scale attribution problems for B026, B047 and B029 are, in his view, more tractable than the attribution in B054, because three listed individuals from collaborations of hundreds or thousands is a very exposed choice.

uncertainties: Whether the committee regards the unresolved pairing mechanism as disqualifying for now, or only as a limit on how the citation is worded.
Whether two laureates (MacDonald and Jarillo-Herrero) or three including Bistritzer is the fairest allocation, and how to treat Cao, Fatemi and earlier theory work outside the credited names.
How much twist-angle disorder and sample-to-sample variability affects the claim that the correlated phases are intrinsic.
I am not able to judge the AMO attribution in B042 and B010 or the astro and particle cases in B026, B029 and B047, so I rely on colleagues there.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my provided profile. I have no known personal or institutional tie to MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero or Bistritzer, nor to the candidates in the alternatives. I chaired the committee for the 2025 prize, which is not a conflict, and my general field overlap with moire and topological materials is scientific rather than personal.
